boundary_rationale: The letter opens with its sender formula, rp:1Cor.1.1 Παῦλος κλητὸς ἀπόστολος, and adds Sosthenes as co-sender. The adscript of 1:2 names the assembly of God at Corinth, sanctified in Christ Jesus, together with those who call on the Lord's name in other places. The prescript ends with the greeting rp:1Cor.1.3 χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη. At 1:4 the speech act changes from salutation to thanks, so the seam falls after 1:3; the RP pilcrow at 1:4 stands at that seam, though the cut rests on the connective-free onset of the letter's finite verbs, the prescript having no finite verb in either witness, the present writer's reading.

boundary_rationale: The body opens at 1:10 with the appeal formula rp:1Cor.1.10 Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, which turns from thanks to petition and asks the readers to speak alike and be knit together in one mind. The ground follows in a report from Chloe's people, rp:1Cor.1.11 Ἐδηλώθη γάρ μοι. The party slogans of 1:12 begin rp:1Cor.1.12 Ἐγὼ μέν εἰμι Παύλου, and the questions of 1:13 and the baptism recollection of 1:14-1:16 answer them. In 1:17 Paul turns from whom he baptized to what he was sent to do, ending on rp:1Cor.1.17 ὁ σταυρὸς τοῦ χριστοῦ. The RP pilcrow at 1:10 stands at the onset, and the RP pilcrow at 1:18 stands after that turn. Confidence is moderate-to-low because 1:17 faces both ways.

boundary_rationale: With rp:1Cor.1.18 Ὁ λόγος γὰρ ὁ τοῦ σταυροῦ the subject moves from Paul's commission to the message itself, folly to those perishing and power to those being saved. A citation follows under rp:1Cor.1.19 Γέγραπται γάρ. A run of questions beginning rp:1Cor.1.20 Ποῦ σοφός presses the point, and the contrast of Jews and Greeks in 1:22-1:24 restates it. The step closes on the maxim rp:1Cor.1.25 Ὅτι τὸ μωρὸν τοῦ θεοῦ σοφώτερον, which rounds off the contrast of wisdom and folly. The RP pilcrow at 1:18 stands at the onset and the RP pilcrow at 1:26 at the close seam, where the form rp:1Cor.1.26 Βλέπετε with γὰρ, imperative on the present writer's reading, turns the argument to the readers' own calling.

boundary_rationale: The argument shifts from third-person thesis to the second person at rp:1Cor.1.26 Βλέπετε γὰρ τὴν κλῆσιν ὑμῶν, ἀδελφοί, an imperative on the present writer's reading; γὰρ links back, and the warrant is the turn to the Corinthians' own calling: few of them wise, powerful or well-born, and God choosing the foolish, weak and despised. boundary_rationale: The step opens with rp:1Cor.2.6 Σοφίαν δὲ λαλοῦμεν ἐν τοῖς τελείοις and develops one claim across its length: a hidden wisdom of God, unknown to the rulers of this age, revealed by the Spirit and discerned by the spiritual. A citation at 2:9 speaks of what eye has not seen. The answer comes in rp:1Cor.2.10 Ἡμῖν δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἀπεκάλυψεν, revelation through the Spirit. The contrast rp:1Cor.2.14 Ψυχικὸς δὲ ἄνθρωπος then sets the unspiritual person against the spiritual. After the question about the Lord's mind the step closes with rp:1Cor.2.16 Ἡμεῖς δὲ νοῦν χριστοῦ ἔχομεν. A Byzantine pilcrow stands at 2:6 as well. At 3:1 a vocative and first-person narrative turn back to the Corinthians as people of the flesh, which closes the step.

The image of milk and solid food in 3:2 and the evidence of jealousy and strife in 3:3 lead back to the party slogans at 3:4. The close rests on those slogans and the turn at 3:5 in both witnesses, and the fleshly charge ending 3:4, rp:1Cor.3.4 οὐχὶ σαρκικοί ἐστε, is RP wording. At 3:5 a question about who Apollos and Paul are opens the account of the servants, so the seam falls after 3:4.

boundary_rationale: The formula rp:1Cor.3.16 Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ναὸς θεοῦ ἐστε addresses the readers as God's temple indwelt by the Spirit. Then 3:17 adds the warning that God will destroy whoever destroys that temple, ending rp:1Cor.3.17 οἵτινές ἐστε ὑμεῖς. The two verses form a compact unit framed by the temple word. An RP pilcrow stands at 3:16, this unit's opening verse, and another at 3:18, the opening verse of the next paragraph, which places it at the seam after this short unit, where a prohibition against self-deception begins; the conditional series running from 3:12 to 3:18 crosses both seams, with rp:1Cor.3.15 Εἴ τινος before this unit, rp:1Cor.3.17 Εἴ τις inside it and rp:1Cor.3.18 εἴ τις after it. Confidence is moderate-to-low: a two-verse unit is short, and the verses can be read as the end of 3:10-3:15 or the head of 3:18-3:23.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Treat 4:17-4:21 as its own travel notice, opening with the sending of Timothy and the planned visit. Rejected: the sending serves the call to imitation in 4:16, and the warning of 4:18-4:21 continues the father's address, so the travel note is embedded in the admonition.
